title: Performance Optimization with OnPush Change Detection

questions.prompt: What does ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush tell Angular to do?

options.text: Never run change detection on the component
Skip checking the component's view unless a specific trigger occurs
Check the component twice per cycle
Disable Zone.js globally

questions.explanation: OnPush prunes checks to only when there's a trackable reason — it doesn't disable change detection entirely.

questions.prompt: Why does mutating an object passed via @Input() fail to update an OnPush component?

options.text: Angular does a deep structural comparison that's too slow
Angular compares inputs by reference, so mutating in place leaves the reference unchanged
OnPush ignores all @Input() changes
Objects cannot be used as inputs

questions.explanation: Reference (Object.is) comparison means you must produce a new object/array for OnPush to detect the change.

questions.prompt: Which of the following trigger a check on an OnPush component? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: An @Input() receives a new reference
An event fires within the component or its children
An async pipe in the template emits a new value
A signal read in the template changes

questions.explanation: New input reference, an internal event, an async pipe emission, a markForCheck() call, or a changed signal all trigger a check.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between markForCheck() and detectChanges()?

options.text: They are identical
markForCheck() schedules a check for the next cycle; detectChanges() runs one immediately and synchronously
detectChanges() only works with signals
markForCheck() disables OnPush

questions.explanation: Prefer markForCheck() (safe, scheduled) unless you specifically need the immediate synchronous run of detectChanges().

questions.prompt: Do signals require OnPush or Zone.js to update the UI?

options.text: Yes, both are required
No — reading a signal in a template registers it as a dependency, so Angular schedules a targeted update independent of Zone.js
Only Zone.js is required
Signals cannot update the UI at all

questions.explanation: Signals wire fine-grained updates automatically, which is why OnPush + Signals is the on-ramp to zoneless Angular.

questions.prompt: The async pipe works seamlessly under OnPush because it internally calls which ChangeDetectorRef method on every emission?
questions.explanation: The async pipe calls markForCheck() for you, so observable data 'just works' with OnPush.

questions.prompt: Since Angular 22, which change detection strategy do components use if they don't set one?

options.text: ChangeDetectionStrategy.Default
ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush
Zone-based checking of the whole tree
No change detection at all

questions.explanation: Since Angular 22, OnPush is the default and the old behavior is called ChangeDetectionStrategy.Eager (Default is deprecated). On Angular 20 and 21 you opt in to OnPush per component.
